stories.title: US launches strikes as Iran says Strait of Hormuz closed
stories.summary: The US military launched fresh strikes on Iran after it struck a container ship, while Tehran said it had again closed the Strait of Hormuz and escalated attacks on US facilities in states across the Gulf. A series of attacks between the US and Iran over the past several days led President Donald Trump to declare the end of a ceasefire meant to halt the fighting that the US and Israel began on 28 February, although Mr Trump has left the door open to continued negotiations. Iran said it closed the strait after firing a warning shot that struck a vessel traveling on an unapproved route. It warned that any retaliation over the incident would be met with a "severe response." US Central Command, however, said commercial vessels continue to transit through the waterway that carried one-fifth of the world's oil and LNG shipments before the war.

stories.title: Boy, 15, dies after getting into difficulty in Lough Ree
stories.summary: A 15-year-old boy has died after getting into difficulty in Lough Ree in Co Westmeath. Emergency services responded to the scene off Carnakilla Point, Glasson, shortly after 7.30pm yesterday. He was pronounced dead and the scene and his body was removed to Regional Hospital Mullingar.

stories.title: NI fire service received over 300 calls on Eleventh Night
stories.summary: The Northern Ireland Fire and Rescue Service (NIFRS) received 303 emergency calls as bonfires were lit for the traditional Eleventh Night celebrations in unionist areas. In one incident firefighters withdrew from a fire in the Cookstown area due to what NIFRS said was a hostile crowd. In Belfast, the fire service dealt with a fire that had spread to a garage on Milner Street. NIFRS said that overall firefighters attended 151 operational incidents and 54 of these were bonfire related.

stories.title: The week that changed everything for Nigel Farage
stories.summary: Of all the crazy weeks in the political life of Nigel Farage, surely this has been his most disturbing. It began with his resignation as a member of the UK parliament; it ended with the murder of his party's justice and immigration spokesperson. In between came the start of a by-election in which his only serious challenger wears a rubbish bin on his head. The most shocking element of all was the murder of Anne Widdicombe, in her home in Dartmoor.

stories.title: Sky-high pitch: The new ways airlines are upselling seats
stories.summary: You step on board the plane with a smile, safe in the knowledge that your 'out of office' will shield you from work for the next little while. You’ve been looking forward to this moment for months - maybe even years - but as you set off to some far-flung destination, your excitement is interrupted by a glance to your left, and a brief glimpse behind the curtain. You know that, on the other side, is how the other half live - fancy food, flowing drinks and cushy seats that become beds. But you're not a first-class kind of person. You're not even business class. So, you sculk to your economy seat and strap yourself in for 16 hours of limited leg-room and plenty of noise.

stories.title: Sticky issues outstanding as the Dáil recess approaches
stories.summary: The Dáil will go into recess on Thursday, but there are plenty of issues that will generate some controversy throughout the summer and beyond. Political Correspondent Mícheál Lehane takes a look at those key issues, from Aughinish to fuel excise cuts, the Triple Lock and more. The report into Aughinish Alumina is just days off completion. It is understood that it will not contain a smoking gun which proves definitively that alumina produced in west Limerick is being used in the Russian war against Ukraine. Instead, the known facts will be presented, and the baton will then be passed on to the European Commission.
